items.title: سنگاپور می‌گوید دو کشتی‌اش در تنگه هرمز هدف قرار گرفتند و یکی از آنها غرق شد
items.summary: سازمان دریایی و بندری سنگاپور اعلام کرده است که دو کشتی کانتینری با پرچم این کشور، روزهای ۱۳ و ۱۴ اکتبر هنگام عبور از تنگه هرمز هدف پرتابه‌های ناشناس قرار گرفته‌اند و یکی از آنها دچار آتش‌سوزی شده و غرق شده است. سنگاپور می‌گوید که هر ۲۱ خدمه این کشتی به سلامت تخلیه شده‌اند. پیشتر نیروی دریایی سپاه پاسداران گفته بود که یک «کشتی کانتینربر متخلف» پس از برخورد با «مین» دریایی در تنگه هرمز آتش‌ گرفت و«غرق» شد.

items.summary: مهدی تارتار، سرمربی پرسپولیس در نشست خبری پس از بازی با خیبر خرم آباد گفت: «به هر حال یک روزهایی توپ وارد دروازه نمی‌شود. بیفوما هفته پیش گل زد، این هفته گل نزد. این طبیعت فوتبال است. به هر حال با تمرین بیشتر و تمرکز بالاتر می‌توانیم بهتر عمل کنیم.»

"And if you elect Democrats, you're fundamentally electing people who will invite criminals into your state, into your communities and make your communities less safe," he added in discussing the upcoming duel for control of Congress. In typically-blue Minnesota, Democratic Lt. Gov. Ukrainian forces discovered the change overnight after experiencing connectivity problems and contacting SpaceX customer support. They were told Starshield service would be restricted on platforms traveling at speeds of 100 miles per hour or higher, the source said. Ukrainian forces have also begun documenting effects on the battlefield. items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV underwent blood tests and a chest X-ray Wednesday following surgery to remove a small nodule on his lung, with his recovery going "as expected," the Vatican announced. The development comes after the Holy See Press Office said "the night passed calmly for the Pope" at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital. The 71-year-old pontiff on Tuesday underwent thoracic surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung with doctors confirming he had lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer, according to a statement released by the Holy See Press Office. "This morning, the Holy Father underwent the blood tests and chest X-ray scheduled after surgery. The results confirm that his postoperative recovery is progressing normally: the values are within the expected range for the type of operation performed," it attributed Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora as saying. POPE LEO DIAGNOSED WITH LUNG CANCER AFTER SURGEONS REMOVE PART OF RIGHT LUNG, VATICAN SAYS "The Holy Father has undergone respiratory physiotherapy and has begun walking around his room. He has resumed eating normally and had breakfast and lunch," their statement added. "His recovery is proceeding as expected." The pope's diagnosis was confirmed through a tissue examination conducted during the operation, consistent with findings from preoperative tests, the Vatican said. items.summary: در حالی که سناتور سوزان کالینز، ایالت مین، از سابقه خود در برابر اتهاماتی مبنی بر اینکه یوهان سباستین دوران گوئررو به دست اداره مهاجرت و گمرک (ICE) امکان مرگ یوهان سباستین دوران گوئررو را فراهم کرده است، در صحنه مناظره عصر سه شنبه اختلاف شدیدی به وجود آمد. تروی جکسون، رقیب دموکرات او، استدلال کرد که کالینز در سه ماهه سالگرد حادثه با تأمین مالی آنچه که او به عنوان یک "آژانس سرکش" توصیف کرد، این برخورد مرگبار را تسهیل کرده است. جکسون با اشاره به حدود 70 میلیارد دلار بودجه برای آژانس های اجرایی مهاجرت که در قانون آمریکای امن گنجانده شده است، گفت: "ببینید، سناتور کالینز هزینه گلوله ها و به دستور دونالد ترامپ را پرداخت. اکنون او اعتبار می خواهد که ماشه را نکشیده است."
items.summary_original: Fierce disagreement broke out on the debate stage on Tuesday evening as Sen. Susan Collins , R-Maine, defended her record against accusations that she had enabled the death of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero at the hands of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Troy Jackson , her Democratic opponent, argued Collins had facilitated the deadly encounter on the three-month anniversary of the incident by funding what he described as a "rogue agency." Hinson remarked on Turek's absences while responding to a question posed to both candidates about Iowa's rising cancer rates. "You have to show up to vote for things like pediatric cancer research, and I've invested in legislation to make sure that we're redirecting those resources to get to where it needs to go to help get to the bottom of this cancer crisis," Hinson said. As Fox News Digital first uncovered , Turek missed 261 votes in Iowa's state legislature from Jan. 12, 2026, through May 3, representing nearly 58% of the total votes during that time. The debate's moderator asked Turek directly why he missed the votes. Tuesday's flight saw 22 migrants land at Kingston’s Norman Manley International Airport in Jamaica. The agreement caps the number of migrants arriving to 25 "per fortnight." Jamaica's Ministry of National Security and Peace and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade released a joint statement clarifying the new program on Tuesday, according to NBC News. items.summary_original: Protesters repeatedly interrupted War Secretary Pete Hegseth’s headline appearance at the Army’s biggest annual conference on Wednesday, calling him a "war criminal" and a "coward" in protest of the Iran war. At least five times in the first half hour of a panel, foul-mouthed anti-war protesters shouted at Hegseth, calling him a "f---ing Nazi" among other insults. Hegseth responded with chuckles and sarcastic comments, at first — but his reactions became increasingly short and irritated as he slammed the "semi-coordinated" attack as one-by-one protesters emerged among the crowd in Washington, D.C. PETE HEGSETH HEADS TO CAPITOL HILL TO DEFEND TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS 60-DAY CONGRESSIONAL DEADLINE LOOMS "You’re not a warrior you’re a coward!" one demonstrator shouted at Hegseth. "Children in Gaza are starving! He is a war criminal!" "She thinks highly of me," the Pentagon chief quipped after one outburst, which led to brief applause from the crowd. The protesters were spread among the room and waited a few minutes between outbursts to interrupt the panel with their anti-war messages. As Hegseth saw a pattern emerging among the outbreaks, he acknowledged: "Appears we have a bit of a tactic." "The protesters are spouting off slogans, Iran really will never have a nuclear weapon," he later added. items.summary_original: The entire Horn of Africa region is said to be on a knife’s edge. As explosions reportedly claimed to be caused by drones hit Ethiopia's capital city in early October, the U.S. Embassy in Addis Ababa warned U.S. citizens of the danger of "long-range attacks." Analysts say there’s a high probability that Ethiopia and Eritrea are about to erupt in a new war, with worrying regional backing for both sides. Former CIA analyst and National Security Council Africa Director Cameron Hudson says the Trump administration needs to become more involved. He told Fox News Digital, "Regional leaders will say privately that they don’t want a regional war. But with so many armed actors and so much meddling going on in each other’s countries, a regional conflagration becomes increasingly likely. It is this kind of miscalculation that the Trump administration needs to be working now to guard against." items.summary_original: An NPR affiliate is apologizing after sponsoring an anarchist book fair that publicly expressed solidarity with defendants prosecuted over a violent attack on a Texas ICE detention facility that left a police officer wounded. New Hampshire Public Radio (NHPR) acknowledged it "erred" by accepting an invitation to sponsor and host a table at the "New Hampshire Anarchist Book Fair" in Hanover, New Hampshire, saying the decision ran afoul of its standards against involvement in activities that could be viewed as political. "NHPR erred in accepting an invitation to sponsor and host a table at the Anarchist Book Festival in Hanover on Saturday," the station said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital by NHPR President and CEO Jim Schachter. "Our code of ethics makes clear that we should not compromise the integrity of our journalism by involvement in anything that can be viewed as political." NPR GETS $80 MILLION GIFT FROM DEMOCRATIC MEGADONOR IN MAJOR BOOST AFTER LOSING GOVERNMENT FUNDING "No one from NHPR's newsroom was aware of or involved in the decision to participate in this event," the statement added. "We remain committed to our mission of independent, trustworthy journalism for everyone in New Hampshire, and we are evaluating our internal processes to ensure mistakes like this don't happen again." items.summary_original: Incumbent Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., who has repeatedly shot down the prospect of mounting a 2028 presidential bid, reiterated his position during a Tuesday night Georgia U.S. Senate debate. Atlanta Journal-Constitution chief political reporter Greg Bluestein pressed Ossoff about the issue during the Atlanta Press Club U.S. Senate debate at the Georgia Public Broadcasting studios. "Senator Ossoff, you've repeatedly said you won't run for president in 2028, but your name continues to surface as a potential contender," Bluestein said, adding, "So will you pledge right now tonight to serve your full six-year term if you win?" "Yes, I will," Ossoff replied. "I have zero interest in running for president. I'm not running for president. I'm running for re-election to the Senate." GOP GOVERNOR CANDIDATE SKIPS DEBATE AGAINST FORMER BIDEN ADVISOR, REPLACED BY EMPTY PODIUM The Democrat faces Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., in the Peach State contest, a Republican congressman who has served in the U.S. House of Representatives since early 2023. Collins pushed back during the debate, saying Ossoff "is running for president" and will "be your DSA candidate," apparently referring to the Democratic Socialists of America. EXCLUSIVE: OSSOFF CHALLENGED TO RETURN EPSTEIN-LINKED DONATION OR RETRACT 'EPSTEIN CLASS' ATTACK Ossoff has served in the U.S. Senate since early 2021. Ilhan Omar ’s husband, Tim Mynett, insisted he has "no concerns" about federal investigations into the Minnesota Democrat’s immigration paperwork after Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents raided the couple’s Washington, D.C., home. "My wife came here when she was 12 years old as a child war refugee," Mynett told Fox News Digital. "No concerns." His comments came the same day that Omar’s relatives were reportedly issued subpoenas, The New York Times reported Tuesday, as part of HSI’s investigation into her immigration paperwork. At least two of Omar's relatives were subpoenaed — one was confirmed to be Omar’s sister, Sahra Noor. Fox News has also learned that subpoenas have been sent to multiple family members of Omar. The subpoenas were issued one day after federal agents searched their Washington, D.C., residence, as first reported by Fox News Digital, as part of an ongoing criminal investigation into her immigration pathway to the United States, two sources familiar with the probe told Fox News Digital. items.summary_original: New York City's lone Republican in the House of Representatives is raising alarms about the far-left Democrats poised to serve alongside her on Capitol Hill next year. "These people are extreme, they're radical, they are dangerous, and they really have no business being in the United States House of Representatives," Rep. Nicole Malliotakis, R-N.Y., told Fox News Digital. "And it scares me that they're going to have access to intelligence." New York City was one of the largest fronts in the nationwide civil war that's gripped the Democratic Party this midterm election cycle . It's where two members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) scored upset primary victories against establishment-backed candidates — in deep-blue seats that mean they are virtually guaranteed to win their general elections in November. DEMOCRATIC CONGRESSMAN WARNS OF 'DANGEROUS' SOCIALIST AGENDA AFTER FAR-LEFT PRIMARY WINS Darializa Avila Chevalier defeated Congressional Hispanic Caucus Chairman Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y., in his Upper Manhattan and Bronx-area district, while New York State Assemblywoman Claire Valdez won an open race for the Brooklyn- and Queens-area district represented by retiring Rep. Nydia Velazquez, D-N.Y. Both Chevalier and Valdez have called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and have called Israel's war on Gaza a "genocide." They wanted to make it an S so that it could be exactly correct. I think it's just terrible that they did it," Trump said. Kathy Hochul and Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman clashed on the debate stage, with the pair trading jabs over President Donald Trump, a recent ICE-involved shooting and inflation. The debate opened with the candidates being asked about the conduct of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which last week drew outrage in New York City following the shooting of a 28-year-old Dominican national whom the Department of Homeland Security said refused to comply with lawful orders during a targeted operation in the Bronx. A 5-year-old boy inside Oscar Bergal's vehicle was unharmed. "Kathy Hochul appealed to ICE to let this criminal out. The question that New Yorkers have to ask is what was this guy doing in New York in the first place? It's because Kathy Hochul has made us a sanctuary state," said Blakeman, a Republican. "Think about it. This guy came into the country illegally. He's been convicted of a crime. He's got pending charges for dealing drugs, poison to our children. And he's a gangbanger. items.summary_original: A bipartisan group of senators is urging Donald Trump to scrap his recently announced diesel deal with Russia, warning it could help President Vladimir Putin finance his war against Ukraine and calling the agreement "a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies." "The Treasury Department’s General License No. 135, which lifts sanctions on Russia’s diesel exports, only provides Putin with more fuel to finance his war machine and enables Russia to continue its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians. Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin’s murderous, illegal war. This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded," the senators asserted in the missive. The letter, which also includes a note of cc to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is signed by GOP Sens. Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Susan Collins of Maine, Alan Stuart Armstrong of Oklahoma, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and John Cornyn of Texas, as well as Democratic Sens. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Dick Durbin of Illinois, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Jack Reed of Rhode Island and Chris Coons of Delaware. Veteran GOP strategist Doug Heye told Fox News Digital that such a strategy at this juncture was "not a surprise." "It happens in midterms when presidents aren’t popular," Heye said. "Add to that the more outlandish things he’s done — often on things that have nothing to do with lowering costs, ending the war with Iran, etc. — this was bound to happen." items.summary_original: Amid growing concerns that the Iran war is drawing away critical U.S. defenses from China's doorstep, the Army's top commander in the Pacific says the forces are using this unexpected opportunity to modernize. Gen. Ronald Clark, commander of U.S. Army Pacific, provided his assessment that diverting Patriot missile defenses to the Iran war has not increased risk to forces in the Indo-Pacific despite concerns about deployments impacting America's readiness for potential conflict with China. "Actually, it's given us an opportunity to modernize our systems here," Clark told Fox News Digital during a small-group interview at the Association of the United States Army's annual conference in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday. Patriot systems have been redeployed from the Indo-Pacific to support operations in the Middle East, while U.S. forces in South Korea have also sent Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) interceptors to the region. An October Congressional Research Service report cited estimates that U.S. forces had expended roughly 1,700 Patriot and 200 THAAD interceptors during the conflict, while the Congressional Budget Office estimated that the military had used between half and two-thirds of certain interceptor inventories. The Pentagon's inspector general has cited strategic inventory shortfalls and manufacturing bottlenecks stemming from the conflict, raising questions about how quickly the U.S. could replenish its defenses in the event of another major confrontation. items.summary_original: Americans aren't just seeing the price tag increase for imported goods. Thanks to President Donald Trump's tariffs, they are now paying more for products made in the U.S.A., according to new research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. In fact, the research finds that prices for many everyday goods would have fallen last year and into early 2026 without Trump's tariffs. The findings offer new evidence of how the sweeping tariff policy, a centerpiece of the president's economic agenda during his second term, have affected Americans’ wallets — and it's only getting worse with just one month until the midterm elections. TRUMP BET TARIFFS WOULD BRING BACK AMERICAN FACTORY JOBS. NEW REPORT SAYS IT DIDN'T WORK Economists had long warned that tariffs would drive up consumer prices, but measuring their precise impact has been difficult as trade policies shifted and companies made decisions about whether to absorb higher costs or pass them along to shoppers. Put simply, the New York Fed found that tariffs kept prices higher on many of the goods Americans buy every day. Without the tariffs, prices across the consumer goods examined for this study would have fallen by early 2026. Instead, they rose. The researchers estimated that tariffs added about 2.9 percentage points to prices across the goods they studied. items.summary_original: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer sees a path to victory for Democrats in November — but one major Republican advantage has him worried. In a letter to his Democratic colleagues, Schumer, D-N.Y., argued that his crop of candidates and Democrats running across the country are winning the messaging battle against the GOP, but asked, "Can Republicans buy the Senate?" "With just three weeks until Election Day, the battle for control of the Senate comes down to one defining question: Will the unprecedented tsunami of Republican money defeat the massive Democratic advantage in candidates, policies, and political climate," Schumer wrote. DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS "There are 22 days until Election Day, and two enormous forces are on a collision course: deep voter dissatisfaction with Republicans and an unprecedented flood of money aimed at overcoming their political liabilities," he continued. "Which force prevails could determine control of the United States Senate." Republicans do have a distinct money advantage and have seen outside groups and President Donald Trump’s MAGA Inc. spending at eye-popping levels across the Senate map. MAGA Inc., for example, has over $400 million at its disposal, according to Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings, and reportedly has plans to spend in key Senate races like Iowa, Ohio and Alaska in the waning weeks of the midterms. items.summary_original: As former Vice President Kamala Harris weighs another White House run in 2028, a longtime advisor is firing back at Democratic strategists and donors who argue she has squandered an opportunity to politically reinvent herself following her 2024 election defeat. Veteran Democratic strategist Maria Cardona, an outside advisor to Harris, pushed back against the criticism highlighted in a new Politico report, defending Harris' policy proposals and campaign activity as Democrats debate whether the former vice president deserves another shot at the White House. Cardona argued the story was "infuriating in its silliness." The report, based on interviews with nearly 20 California-based Democratic donors and strategists, highlighted growing skepticism among some party insiders about Harris' political future and whether she has done enough to distinguish herself from her unsuccessful 2024 campaign. Longtime Democratic strategist Doug Herman, a veteran of former President Barack Obama’s 2008 and 2012 campaigns, told Politico that Harris "totally blew it ... She hasn’t gotten into the mix." items.summary_original: A federal appeals court on Tuesday ruled that a federal ban on gun possession by convicted felons cannot be constitutionally applied to some people whose prior offenses did not involve violence or threats indicating a risk of misusing firearms . The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit issued two rulings clarifying when the federal prohibition on gun possession by convicted felons can be enforced under the Second Amendment. The court, which includes several judges appointed by President Donald Trump, upheld the firearms restriction against a man with a conviction stemming from a carjacking but ruled that the ban could not be applied to another man based on his prior drunk-driving convictions. One of the cases decided on Tuesday involved James Bost, who pleaded guilty to terroristic threats, criminal conspiracy, false imprisonment and simple assault in Pennsylvania state court following a 2002 carjacking. items.title_original: Greta Thunberg joins massive French student protests as cars burn, police fire tear gas
items.summary: گرتا تونبرگ، فعال اقلیمی، روز سه شنبه پس از هفته ها درگیری خشونت آمیز با پلیس، هزاران بازداشت و تعطیلی گسترده مدارس به دلیل درخواست اصلاحات آموزشی، به معترضان دانشجویی در فرانسه پیوست. به گزارش رویترز، این فعال 23 ساله سوئدی در خارج از دبیرستانی در سن دنیس در شمال پاریس ظاهر شد، جایی که دانش آموزان خواستار معلمان بیشتر، امکانات بهتر و روزهای تحصیلی کوتاه تر بودند. به گفته مقامات فرانسوی، از زمان آغاز اعتراضات در ماه سپتامبر، بیش از 6800 نفر بازداشت شده اند. تظاهرکنندگان در شهرهای سراسر فرانسه آتش زدند، سنگرها برپا کردند و با پلیس ضد شورش مقابله کردند، اگرچه بسیاری از اعتراضات مسالمت آمیز باقی مانده است. با شورش دانش‌آموزان بر سر تحصیل، فرانسه دوباره منفجر می‌شود.
items.summary_original: Climate activist Greta Thunberg joined student protesters in France on Tuesday after weeks of violent confrontations with police, thousands of arrests and widespread school closures over demands for education reform. The 23-year-old Swedish activist appeared outside a high school in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, where students were demanding more teachers, better facilities and shorter school days, Reuters reported. More than 6,800 people have been detained since the protests began in September, according to French authorities. Demonstrators have set fires, erected barricades and confronted riot police in cities across France, although many protests have remained peaceful. FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION Thunberg, who rose to prominence organizing school strikes over climate change , criticized the French government's response to the demonstrations. "We are inspired by the young people who are demanding their basic rights," Thunberg told reporters, according to Reuters. She also described the police response as "extremely violent." About 161,500 people marched across France on Tuesday, including 41,500 in Paris, according to Interior Ministry figures. The Education Ministry said 214 schools were closed. items.summary: گروهی از زندانیان سیاسی در زندان‌های مختلف جمهوری اسلامی در پیامی به مناسبت زادروز شهبانو فرح پهلوی، او را «نماد فرهنگ و هنر ایران» دانستند. این زندانیان سیاسی ابراز امیدواری کردند که روزی جشن زادروز شهبانو فرح پهلوی در ایرانی آزاد و آباد برگزار شود.

items.title: در یمن جنگی با پیامدهای جهانی در جریان است
items.summary: از خطوط مقدم نبرد در استان لحج تا بیمارستان‌های مملو از مجروح در عدن، جنگ یمن بار دیگر وارد مرحله‌ای تعیین‌کننده شده است. حوثی‌ها که هم‌زمان کشتیرانی جهانی و عربستان سعودی را تحت فشار قرار داده‌اند، اکنون در مرکز رویارویی گسترده‌تری قرار دارند که از تهران تا ریاض امتداد یافته و بر امنیت انرژی، ثبات منطقه و زندگی میلیون‌ها یمنی سایه انداخته است.

items.title: لیگ نخبگان آسیا؛ دبل سردار آزمون الاتحاد را زمین‌گیر کرد، الهلال السد را شکست داد
items.summary: در هفته دوم لیگ نخبگان آسیا، شباب‌الاهلی امارات با درخشش سردار آزمون، الاتحاد عربستان سعودی را ۲ بر یک شکست داد. آزمون هر دو گل تیمش را به ثمر رساند و رضا غندی‌پور که از دقیقه ۱۶ وارد زمین شده بود، پاس گل دوم او را داد. سعید عزت‌اللهی نیز ۹۰ دقیقه برای شباب‌الاهلی بازی کرد.

items.summary_original: A year has passed since President Donald Trump made history by brokering a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, setting in motion an ambitious peace plan aimed at bringing lasting stability to the region. In the days and months since the ceasefire and Trump’s 20-point peace plan took hold, progress has drawn support from across the globe — including from unexpected quarters. Senior advisor to the Board of Peace Josh Gruenbaum told Fox News Digital that the success of the last 12 months was largely attributable to President Donald Trump’s leadership and commitment to seeking peace. TRUMP-BACKED BOARD OF PEACE, ISRAEL 'WILL TAKE ACTION' IF HAMAS REMAINS OUT OF COMPLIANCE: NETANYAHU ADVISOR "The unlock was somebody who came in, who really knew the file because they had the chance to study it and understand it," Gruenbaum said. Trump and his team, including U.S. special envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff, U.S. special envoy for Peace Jared Kushner and Secretary of State Marco Rubio , "created working relationships with regional actors with trust, overlaid with peace through strength," while also forcing Hamas to finally understand that "this was either going to end the very hard way for them, or there was an off-ramp and a way to do this in a more dignified way, which is what the 20-point plan was." items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV underwent a procedure at Agostino Gemelli University Hospital in Rome to remove a small nodule on his lung Tuesday, the Vatican said. The 71-year-old pontiff underwent thoracic surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung and doctors confirmed he had lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer, according to a statement released by the Holy See Press Office . The diagnosis was confirmed through a tissue examination conducted during the operation, consistent with findings from preoperative tests, the Vatican said. The pope spent approximately three hours in the operating room, although the surgery itself lasted about 90 minutes. Doctors said the procedure was successful and there were no complications. POPE LEO ANNOUNCES TUMOR ON LUNG, SURGERY PLANNED IN 'NEXT FEW DAYS' Leo awoke normally following surgery and, after a brief observation period, returned to his room on the hospital's 10th floor, according to the statement from Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora. "Doctors found a small lump in the lung," Leo said after an Angelus address at St. Peter's Square on Monday. "It was identified at a very early stage and well situated." "The doctors consider it appropriate to intervene and so, following their advice, I decided to have surgery to remove it," he continued. "The surgery is already scheduled for the next few days. items.summary_original: NATO's top military commander warned Monday that what he called the "lethal alliance" would destroy "anything and everything" supporting an attack on allied territory and "break" enemy warfighting systems to thwart any potential future Russian assault. "Should the adversary choose to press the attack or commit his reserves, we will break the warfighting system engaged against us," U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland , in an apparent warning to Moscow. "This includes not just the attacking force itself, but anything and everything that supports, sustains, and controls that force," he said during a panel titled "Theory of Victory: How Do We Achieve Military Success Against Russia in Deterrence and Defence?" on the first day of the forum. US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS Grynkewich, NATO's supreme allied commander in Europe, also outlined a three-pronged strategy of "blocking, blunting and breaking" enemy forces, making clear that while NATO is a defensive alliance, it is prepared to respond decisively to an assault on any of its 32 members. "If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight," he said. "We will stop the attack and deny them the ability to achieve their objectives, whatever those might be. items.summary: کارل بوشبی، ماجراجو، سرانجام پس از 28 سال سفر در سراسر جهان، پا به خاک بریتانیا گذاشت. در 5 اکتبر، او اعلام کرد که کانال مانش را از فرانسه به انگلستان شنا کرده است. در حالی که در دوور استراحت می کرد، گفت: "من به یونیون جک که بیرون از این هتل در حال پرواز است خیره شده ام. در طول روزها پرچم های زیادی دیده ام، اما آن یکی خاص است." او در رسانه های اجتماعی یکی از اولین وعده های غذایی خود را به اشتراک گذاشت، در حالی که از خوردن دوباره ماهی و چیپس بریتانیایی بسیار خوشحال بود. دیل «ریش خاکستری» سندرز عنوان مسن‌ترین فرد برای راهپیمایی در مسیر آپالاچیان در 91 سالگی را پس می‌گیرد سفر او هنوز به پایان نرسیده است. او امیدوار است تا پایان ماه به خط پایان برسد - خانه مادرش در هال. به گفته وب سایت او، او در دهه 1990 کارت تولدی از پدرش دریافت کرد که در مورد دو سرباز که بر سر یک شاهکار غیرممکن دعوا می کردند.

On Oct. 5, he announced he swam the English Channel , from France to England. While resting in Dover, he said, "I’m staring at the Union Jack flying outside this hotel. I’ve seen many flags over the days, but that one is special." On social media he shared one of his first meals back, overjoyed to have authentic British fish and chips again. According to his website , he received a birthday card in the 1990s from his father about two soldiers arguing over an impossible feat, walking from London to New York via the Bering Strait. Karl grabbed a map and drew a single line, knowing he found his life’s mission. Asked whether Ukraine would honor the ceasefire, Zelenskyy answered, "Of course," insisting that Kyiv had already refrained from striking Russian energy facilities overnight. Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, Netanyahu, has overseen the country’s transformation into a free-market, high-tech economy and a regional military powerhouse. Zvika Klein, editor-in-chief of The Jerusalem Post, told Fox News Digital that people under 20 "don’t even know an Israel without him being prime minister," aside from the brief period from 2021 to 2022 when a government led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid was in power for over a year. The two are running again on a joint slate in the upcoming elections. "The job is not finished. On the one hand, you have Netanyahu, who from the first moment, two days after Oct. 7, said that we are going to change the Middle East ," he said. items.summary: پاپ لئو چهاردهم مجازات اعدام را "غیرقابل قبول" محکوم کرد زیرا پنتاگون به دلیل برنامه ریزی برای پخش زنده یک اعدام در اواخر سال جاری با انتقاد روبرو می شود. لئو، اولین پاپ آمریکایی، روز شنبه در پستی در شبکه های اجتماعی به مناسبت روز جهانی مبارزه با مجازات اعدام، مخالفت خود را با مجازات اعدام به اشتراک گذاشت. لئو با استناد به دکترین کاتولیک اصلاح شده در زمان سلف خود، پاپ فرانسیس، تاکید کرد که مجازات اعدام، کرامت انسانی را نقض می کند. "مجازات اعدام غیرقابل پذیرش است زیرا حمله به مصونیت و حیثیت افراد است. منفعت عمومی را می توان حفظ کرد و الزامات عدالت را می توان بدون توسل به مجازات اعدام برآورده کرد: سیستم های موثر بازداشت توسعه یافته اند که از شهروندان محافظت می کند و در عین حال مجرمان را کاملاً محروم نمی کند.
items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV condemned the death penalty as "inadmissible" as the Pentagon faces criticism over plans to livestream an execution later this year. Leo, the first American pope, shared his opposition to capital punishment Saturday in a social media post marking World Day Against the Death Penalty. Citing Catholic doctrine revised under his predecessor, Pope Francis, Leo emphasized that the death penalty violates human dignity. "The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo wrote on X. "#NoDeathPenalty," he added in the post. items.summary_original: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died when a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the United Nations' migration agency. The vessel was carrying 305 people from Djibouti toward Yemen when it capsized Thursday night or early Friday near Guhere, north of Obock, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Sunday. At least 84 people remained missing as of Sunday, while more than 80 survived. All the survivors were Ethiopian nationals , according to the agency. "No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way," IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a statement. I am asking governments and donors to act before the next boat goes down," Pope added. The confirmed death toll includes only victims buried by authorities in Djibouti and could rise as additional bodies are verified, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac told The Associated Press. items.summary_original: Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports . The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector. The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300. SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis. "Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu , senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday. "The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned. Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove , former NATO supreme allied commander Europe and head of U.S. European Command, told Fox News Digital that Washington also risks undermining Ukraine's war effort by striking a deal with what he called "the enemy." "And so we are cutting a deal with the enemy," Breedlove said, warning that "all of this money will go into fueling Mr. Putin's continued attacks in Ukraine." The Russian government said Saturday it had partially lifted a ban on diesel exports with immediate effect, following the new agreement between Putin and Trump for Russia to supply the U.S. and global markets, Reuters reported. As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Trump's package calls for the release of 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace," followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes afterward. items.summary_original: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed Oct. 8 that U.S. and Israeli strikes had failed to undermine Iran's domestic security forces, praising police personnel for resisting attacks launched in February under Operations Epic Fury and Roaring Lion. Khamenei's remarks on X also came as the U.S. Army released a new battlefield identification guide to help American troops recognize members of Iran's conventional military, known as the Artesh, whose ground forces were estimated by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security in June at 350,000 personnel. "The criminal US-Zionist enemy's desperate efforts and malicious attacks on the pillars of social order and security, which are unparalleled throughout history, have not caused the courageous personnel of the Police Force to waver even a fraction in their mission," Khamenei wrote in a statement. Khamenei specifically praised Iran's Law Enforcement Command, known as FARAJA, accusing the United States and Israel of targeting the institution responsible for maintaining domestic order. "The focus and persistence of the criminal US-Zionist enemy in striking at the Police Force at its various levels, from its highest command levels down to those who are on the frontline, has only served to underscore the paramount importance of this institution more than ever," he wrote. items.summary_original: More than two decades after being elected to what was supposed to be a four-year term, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has once again postponed elections, extending a nearly 20-year wait for voters to choose a new legislature. Abbas issued a decree Friday pushing Palestinian Legislative Council elections from next month to Sept. 11, 2027, according to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA. Presidential elections , which have not been held since Abbas' 2005 victory, are also scheduled for that date. The delay allows Palestinian leaders to remain in power without facing voters and could further damage the credibility of the Palestinian Authority, which has faced criticism over corruption and its security cooperation with Israel. NICARAGUA'S ORTEGA SAYS COUNTRY WILL 'NEVER AGAIN' HOLD ELECTIONS, SHUTTING OUT OPPOSITION The Palestinian Authority, dominated by Abbas' Fatah party, governs parts of the West Bank under agreements reached in the 1990s. Palestinian officials cited conditions in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and east Jerusalem as reasons for postponing the vote. The Palestine Liberation Organization's Executive Committee, which Abbas heads, claimed Israel had blocked election materials and international observers from entering Gaza, according to The Associated Press. And had an ominous warning, "What you’re seeing in London and other European cities can easily happen in the U.S… These cultural shifts will all come to America, unless American leaders are willing to fight back." Italian Prime Minister Georgia Meloni defended the decree on X , calling the new rules "Tools of common sense that do not divide, but truly help to integrate, avoiding ghetto classes and giving all students the same opportunities. items.summary_original: As Israel prepared to assassinate Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in September 2024, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his senior defense officials disagreed over whether to notify the Biden administration ahead of the operation, fearing Washington could try to stop the mission, according to Wall Street Journal editorial writer Elliot Kaufman and a second source familiar with the deliberations. "140%, they won't approve of the mission," Netanyahu told senior Israeli defense officials, according to Kaufman, co-author of " In the War Room: The Inside Story of Israel's Fight Against Hamas and the Iranian Axis ," who recounted the exchange in an interview with Fox News Digital. Then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant and IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi favored informing Washington, believing the Americans might support a strike against a Hezbollah leader linked to the deaths of U.S. service members, according to Kaufman. Netanyahu, however, warned that then-U.S. National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan would "jump out of his skin" if he learned of the plans. The disagreement reflected a widening divide between Jerusalem and Washington over Israel's military campaign against Iran's regional proxies, as the Biden administration sought to prevent the fighting from escalating into a broader regional war. items.summary_original: Student protests over crumbling schools despite billions in public spending are fueling a broader crisis in France, and experts warn that the country's mounting financial troubles, President Emmanuel Macron's weakened political center and radical movements are pushing the unrest far beyond its original educational grievances. ET، در عمق 7.8 مایلی، نزدیک پیتالوزا آریبا، پاناما. پس لرزه ای به بزرگی 5.5 ریشتر به وقوع پیوست که کانون آن تقریباً 50 مایلی شرق زمین لرزه اولیه بود. کانال پاناما اعلام کرد که پس از زمین لرزه روز جمعه عملیات به طور عادی ادامه دارد و پروتکل های اضطراری فعال شده و تیم های فنی تاسیسات را برای خسارات احتمالی بازرسی می کنند. مقامات کانال گفتند که اولویت آنها تضمین ایمنی کارگران، کشتی‌ها، خدمه و جوامع مجاور با ادامه ارزیابی‌ها است.
items.summary_original: A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat. The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, at a depth of 7.8 miles, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama. A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake. The Panama Canal said operations were continuing normally following Friday's earthquake, with emergency protocols activated and technical teams inspecting facilities for possible damage. Canal officials said their priority was ensuring the safety of workers, vessels, crews and nearby communities as assessments continued. MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica , according to Reuters. Tsunami officials warned that waves reaching 3 to 10 feet above tide levels were possible along some coastal areas of Panama, while parts of Ecuador could experience waves of approximately 1 to 3 feet. Smaller tsunami waves of less than 1 foot above tide levels were forecast for coastal areas of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru. The Norwegian Nobel Committee honored Pillay, 85, for her contributions to international law and efforts to hold perpetrators of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide accountable. items.summary_original: Thousands of demonstrators poured into the streets of Brussels on Friday, at times clashing with police officers, to protest the Belgian government's budget-tightening measures and the overall rise in the cost of living. Dozens of protesters, most of them young and dressed in black with masks over their faces, were seen throwing rocks and firecrackers at police at the central Brussels railway station, The Associated Press reported. They also set several fires, with photos showing a man lighting an electric scooter ablaze. MAY DAY PROTESTS ACROSS EUROPE AND ASIA TURN INTO ANTI-AMERICAN, ANTI-ISRAEL POLITICAL BATTLEGROUNDS Riot police responded by deploying tear gas canisters and shooting water cannons, tactics that dispersed the crowds. The chaos in the streets contributed to increased traffic across the Belgian capital. Police said the unrest was caused by people unaffiliated with the anti-austerity demonstration, which drew an estimated 30,000 participants, the AP reported. Two of Belgium’s largest labor unions organized Friday’s daylong national strike, with a separate public-sector walkout planned for Monday. Union leaders also distanced themselves from the unrest, saying those responsible were not affiliated with their movement. THINK YOUR STATE IS EXPENSIVE? items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.

items.title: 'کودتای خزنده' در سپاه؛ نوار صوتی جلسه‌ای محرمانه در زمان جنگ
items.summary: با گذشت چهل سال از آغاز جنگ ایران و عراق، هنوز اطلاعات مرتبط با مقاطع مهمی از جنگ، از آرشیوهای محرمانه خارج نشده است. یکی از جلسات مهمی که در آن فرماندهی جنگ مورد انتقاد سپاهیان ناراضی قرار می‌گیرد، اوایل آذر ۶۳ برگزار می‌شود که در دهه‌های اخیر، رسانه‌های حکومتی ایران روایت‌های پراکنده و به‌شدت تحریف شده‌ای را از آن منتشر کرده‌اند.
